\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}]
in the commutative sub-algebra
\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}]\subseteq\mathcal{A}
is normal.

Definition 2.14

(Structure constants)
.

For an algebra
\mathcal{A}
, let
B=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{j}\}_{(j\in J)}\subset\mathcal{A}
be a basis.
Then any product
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{i}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{j}\in\mathcal{A}
of basis elements has an expansion

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{i}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{j}=\sum_{k\in J}\mathchoice{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-8.27415pt{B}\kern 4.20052pt{k}}}_{{\kern-3.81163pt\kern 4.20052pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-8.27415pt{B}\kern 4.20052pt{k}}}_{{\kern-3.81163pt\kern 4.20052pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-5.47835pt{B}\kern 2.53687pt{k}}}_{{\kern-2.14798pt\kern 2.53687pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-4.75354pt{B}\kern 1.81206pt{k}}}_{{\kern-1.42317pt\kern 1.81206pt{ij}}}}\;\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}_{k}.

The
\mathchoice{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-8.27415pt{B}\kern 4.20052pt{k}}}_{{\kern-3.81163pt\kern 4.20052pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-8.27415pt{B}\kern 4.20052pt{k}}}_{{\kern-3.81163pt\kern 4.20052pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-5.47835pt{B}\kern 2.53687pt{k}}}_{{\kern-2.14798pt\kern 2.53687pt{ij}}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}}\gamma^{{\kern-4.75354pt{B}\kern 1.81206pt{k}}}_{{\kern-1.42317pt\kern 1.81206pt{ij}}}}\in\mathbb{C}
are called the

structure constants

[
55
]

of the algebra
\mathcal{A}
w.r.t. the basis
B
.

For practical computations, knowledge of the structure constants in Definition
2.14

is important, as they determine the multiplicative structure of the algebra through
the bi-linearity of the product
[
55
]
, and are sufficient to compute any product.

Remark 2.15
.

For the bounded elements of the algebra, with a bound
C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}
as defined in
Definition
2.12
, set
\widehat{C}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}=\inf\{C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mid C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\text{ is a bound}\}

and
\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}\mid\widehat{C}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}=0\}

to be the
ideal
(cf. Definition
2.12
) of elements where the infimum over all
possible bounds vanishes. In case
\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}\}
, the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}
is called

non-degenerate
. Otherwise, for
\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}\neq\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}\}
, consider the
quotient *-algebra
\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}
, where the state corresponding to
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}
then is
non-degenerate.

As later (cf. Proposition
2.61
)
\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\|_{\infty}=\widehat{C}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}

will be taken to define the operator
norm, the quotient construction makes sure that this is indeed a norm. This removes

superfluous
elements from the algebra.

The following Proposition
2.16
gives a few equivalent indicators for the
situation described in Remark
2.15
, cf.
[
98
]
.

Proposition 2.16
.

Let
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
be a probability algebra.
Then the following statements are equivalent:

•

\widehat{C}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}=0
or
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}
(cf. Remark
2.15
).

•

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{c}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{c}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{c}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{c}})=0
for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{c}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{c}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{c}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{c}}\in\mathcal{A}
.

•

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})=0
for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}
.

In case
\mathcal{A}
is Abelian, or the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is
tracial
,
these statements are also equivalent with the following:

•

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=0
.

•

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})=0
for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}
.

In case
\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}\neq\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}\}
, we shall henceforth tacitly assume that the
factorisation described in Remark
2.15
has been performed,
and that in this case
\mathcal{A}
has been replaced by
\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{I}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}
,
so that the statements in Proposition
2.16
apply only to
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
.

The foregoing framework will make it possible that many standard
constructions and concepts from commutative probability carry
over naturally to the non-commutative realm, albeit
with additional care due to the non-commuting product.

As will be seen later, certain probability algebras — e.g. all finite
dimensional ones — are generated by their projections
\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{A})
,
cf. Example
5
. These are also important as they can be given
an additional interpretation, namely with a projection representing an
event

— see also Example
5
and Proposition
2.19
—
with a probability assigned to it; this assignment is also called the
Born
rule:

Definition 2.17

(Probability — Born’s rule)
.

The
probability
, in the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
, of observing an event
described by a projection
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{A})
is defined as

\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}).

(2.3)

The following facts are directly implied by this and Definition
2.12
:

Proposition 2.18

(Events)
.

As for any positive element
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\geq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\geq 0
,
this implies that for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\leq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\leq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}).

Thus for a projection
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{A})
, one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp}\in\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}]
, and as

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}\leq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\leq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}
, this implies

0\leq\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})\leq 1\;\text{ and }\;\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})+\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp})=1.

For any character
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}
on
\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}]
one has
0\leq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})\leq 1
, and hence

\text{ either }\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=0\,\text{ or }\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=1,\;\text{ i.e. }\,\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})\subseteq\{0,1\}.

The case
\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\{0\}
occurs for the constant
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\equiv\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
(the impossible
event), and the case
\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\{1\}
occurs for the constant
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\equiv\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}

(the sure event); for any other (proper) projection

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}<\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}<\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}
one has
\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\{0,1\}
.

Thus the observation
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}\right\rangle=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}})=1
can be interpreted
in such way that the
event

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}
has been observed. It is a
sharp

observable, there is no doubt that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}
has been observed.
The probability of this happening was
\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})
before the observation,
whereas the probability of
observing the
opposite event

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp}
was
\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp})=1-\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}})
;
but
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp}
with
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}^{\perp}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}})=0

has not been observed.

The deliberations in Example
5
may be continued in an abstract setting:

Proposition 2.19

(Boolean Algebra)
.

Let
R\subset\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{A})
, with
R:=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{j}\},j\in J
be a collection of
commuting projections including the identity
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}
—

\forall i,j\in J:\,[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{i},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{j}]=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
, cf. Example
5
—
so that
\mathbb{C}[R]\in\mathcal{A}
is a commutative probability sub-algebra.
Define for any projections
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{C}[R])
as “
meet
” or “
and
”
or “
intersection
” or “
infimum
”
the symbol
\sqcap
; and as “
join
” or “
or
”
or “
union
” or “
supremum
” the symbol
\sqcup
;
and as “
complement
” or “
negation
” the symbol
\neg
, by setting:

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}\sqcap\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2}

\displaystyle:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2};

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}\sqcup\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2}

\displaystyle:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}+\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2}-\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{2};

\displaystyle\neg\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}

\displaystyle:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{p}}_{1}^{\perp}.

Then
\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{C}[R])
together with these operations is a
Boolean algebra
,
with greatest element
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}
and least element
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
.
Together with the probability assignment from Definition
2.17
, this is a
basic
Kolmogorovean probability space
.

The part to make this Boolean algebra into a
\sigma
-Boolean algebra when
J
is an
infinite set, so that
the probability space can be defined on a
\sigma
-algebra, is a certain completeness
property, a subject not to be addressed here. But for finite dimensional algebras,
when
J
is necessarily of finite cardinality,
this is not needed, and the construction in Proposition
2.19
is a proper (finite,
but
pointless
)
Kolmogorovean probability space, with the projections being analogues of the elements
of the algebra of sets. Of course, it is well known that by Stone’s theorem any such Boolean
algebra is isomorphic to a field of subsets of some set.

In continuation of Remark
2.10
and Proposition
2.19
, one may make the following

Remark 2.20

(Matrix Observable, Projective Measurement)
.

Consider an observable
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\in\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})_{sa}
(
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
) with spectral decomposition

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}
with
\lambda_{k}\in\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})\subset\mathbb{R}

and thus commuting orthogonal projections
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}
, which form a
partition of unity

\sum_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}
, cf. Remark
2.10
. The possible observations are the
elements of the spectrum (cf. Proposition
2.8
),
sharp observations
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\lambda_{k}
,
with the probability of observing
\lambda_{k}
as
\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=\lambda_{k}):=p_{k}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k})
. Observing
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\lambda_{k}

carries the same information as the observation
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k})=1
, as necessarily
for
j\neq k
one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{j})=0
, and we know that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}
has the value
\lambda_{k}
.

Such
sharp
observations of projections
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}})
are also called a

projective measurement
,
and are the basic building blocks for all sharp observations. In case
\lambda_{k}
is a simple
eigenvalue and hence the eigenspace is one-dimensional with unit eigenvector
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}\in\mathbb{C}^{n}
,
the (minimal) projector is given by
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
. In this case the observation
can be written as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}
(cf. Definition
2.23
).
And in case of
a multiple eigenvalue with an eigenspace
V_{k}\subseteq\mathbb{C}^{n}
of say dimension
d
, one can
find an ortho-normal basis
\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k_{j}}\}_{j=1\dots d}
of
V_{k}
, so that the projector then
may be written as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}=\sum_{j}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k_{j}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k_{j}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
. Thus the expected value can be written as

\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}\,\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=\lambda_{k})=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}p_{k}
.

Definition 2.21

(Projection Valued Measure (PVM))
.

The assignment
\Uppi_{M}:2^{\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})}\ni\{\lambda_{k}\}\mapsto\ \mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\lambda_{k}}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))

is an example of a
projection valued measure (PVM)
on the set of all
subsets of
\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})\subset\mathbb{R}
.
It satisfies

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}))=

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}},\quad\text{ and for disjoint }\;E_{1},E_{2}\subseteq\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}):

(2.4)

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1}\uplus E_{2})=

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1})+\Uppi_{M}(E_{2}).

(2.5)

This implies
\Uppi_{M}(\emptyset)=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}
, and for not necessarily disjoint
E_{1},E_{2}\subset\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})
:

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1}\cup E_{2})=

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1})+\Uppi_{M}(E_{2})-\Uppi_{M}(E_{1}\cap E_{2}),\;\text{ and }

(2.6)

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1}\cap E_{2})=

\displaystyle\Uppi_{M}(E_{1})\Uppi_{M}(E_{2})=\Uppi_{M}(E_{2})\Uppi_{M}(E_{1}).

(2.7)

From Eq.(
2.7
) follows that the minimal projections
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\lambda_{k}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}
in
the PVM are orthogonal to each other, and that they commute in general. Thus

\spn\{\Uppi_{M}(E)\mid E\subseteq\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})\}=\mathbb{C}[\{\Uppi_{M}(E)\mid E\subseteq\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})\}]=\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}]\subset\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})

is a commutative sub-algebra of
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
.

Together with the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))

this leads to a discrete measure

2^{\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})}\ni\{\lambda_{k}\}\mapsto\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\lambda_{k}})=\mathbb{P}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\lambda_{k}})=p_{k}\in\mathbb{R}
.

That in the above Definition
2.21
the PVM was chosen to be defined on the singletons

\{\lambda_{k}\}\in 2^{\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})}
was due to the development indicated in
Remark
2.20
, via Eq.(
2.5
) it can then be defined for
any subset
E\subset\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})
. In fact, the
\sigma
-algebra
2^{\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})}

is also a special case:

Remark 2.22

(PVM on any
\sigma
-algebra)
.

The more general definition of a PVM as in Definition
2.21
is that there is a

\sigma
-algebra
\mathfrak{Y}\subseteq 2^{Y}
of subsets of some set
Y
, so that
with subsets
E_{1},E_{2}\in\mathfrak{Y}
the Eqs.(
2.4
) and (
2.5
) hold.

For a finite dimensional algebra as
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
and any disjoint
cover
\biguplus_{k}E_{k}=Y
,
(E_{k}\cap E_{j}=\emptyset,E_{k}\in\mathfrak{Y})
,
there can obviously be only finitely many non-zero projections
in the sum in
\Uppi_{M}(Y)=\sum_{k}\Uppi_{M}(E_{k})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}
. So taking only minimal
projections (cf. Definition
2.12
and Remark
2.20
) in the PVM for this
equation (corresponding to a maximal disjoint cover),
one can find a finite set
X
where the singletons
\{x\},(x\in X)
, correspond
in a bijective fashion to the members of this maximal disjoint cover.
The
\sigma
-algebra
2^{X}
— generated by the singletons — then is in
one-to-one correspondence with
\mathfrak{Y}
, so that the minimal projections are
images of singletons
\{x\}\in 2^{X}
. This is the setting which
will be assumed in the following. In Definition
2.21
one has
X=\sigma(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})\subset\mathbb{R}
.

The set
X

is often called the
outcome space
, meaning that when
\Uppi_{M}(\{x_{k}\})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{x_{k}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}
has been observed, i.e.
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k})=1
for an observation

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}
, the outcome of the observation is
x_{k}\in X
.
Note that for the mutually orthogonal projections (
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{j}=\updelta_{jk}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k}
)
in the PVM
\Uppi_{M}
, and considering Proposition
2.18
, from
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{k})=1
follows
that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{j})=0
for all
j\neq k
; where
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{j}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{x_{j}}=\Uppi_{M}(\{x_{j}\})
.

Definition 2.23

(Density Matrix, Vector State)
.

Recalling Examples
4
and
5
and the definition of the Frobenius state

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{F}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})={\mathchoice{{{{\raise 2.58334pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\kern-1.50696pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-1.29167pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\textstyle n$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.01385pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle n$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle n$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle n$}}}}}}}}\,\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})
, one sees that any normalised state (cf. Definition
2.1
)

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
may be written as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})
.
The matrix
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}
has to be self-adjoint, positive, and of unit trace:
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}})=\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}})=\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}})=1
. Such a matrix is called a
density
matrix.
It thus has a spectral decomposition (cf. Remark
2.10
)

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}=\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}_{j}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}_{j}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
with unit eigenvectors

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}_{j}
and eigenvalues
\alpha_{j}\geq 0
,
\tr(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}})=\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}=1
.
The set of all such density matrices is denoted by

\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})):=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})_{+}\mid\tr\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}=1\}.

(2.8)

Dealing with a matrix algebra like
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
, we may use a different notation for the
same state, depending on the situation; e.g. with
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
given,
one has for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\in\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\right\rangle_{F}=\tr\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=n\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{F}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}).

In case of a simple eigenvalue
\lambda_{k}
, the above observation
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}

in Remark
2.20
is

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\tr((\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}
with
density matrix
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}_{k}=(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}})
.
In case of a multiple eigenvalue with eigenspace
V_{k}
, there is a unit vector
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}\in V_{k}

such that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\tr((\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}
.
The associated density matrix for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{k}
is then either
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}_{k}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
or
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}_{k}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{w}}_{k}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
, a
vector state
.
On an Abelian matrix algebra such as
\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}]
from Example
6
,
such a vector state is indeed a multiplicative
character if
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{v}}_{k}
is an eigenvector of
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}
.

For vector states like
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
, one often calls the vector
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}
itself the
state. Indeed, this is the origin of the name “state”, as the vector
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}
can be regarded
as the state of some system modelled on
\mathbb{C}^{n}
.

Proposition 2.24

(Set of Density Matrices, Mixed State)
.

The set of density matrices
\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
(cf. Definition
2.23
) is closed and convex.
Geometrically speaking, it is the intersection of two closed convex sets, the positive cone

\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})_{+}
(cf. Definition
2.12
and Example
5
) and the hyperplane

\mathcal{T}=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}\mid\tr\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}=1\}
:

\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))=\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})_{+}\cap\mathcal{T}.

(2.9)

Denoting density matrices of rank
r
by

\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{r}=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))\mid\rank\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}=r\}
, where
r=1,\dots,n
,
one has the
disjoint union

\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))=\biguplus_{r=1}^{n}\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{r}.

(2.10)

The extreme points of
\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
are the rank one matrices

\mathrm{ext}(\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})))=\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{1}=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}\in\mathbb{C}^{n},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}=1\},

(2.11)

they are also called
pure
or
vector states
.

According to the Krein-Milman theorem — this also follows from the spectral
decomposition in Definition
2.23
—
a general density matrix
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
is the convex combination
of vector or pure states
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}_{j}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}_{j}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{1}
,
it is often called a
mixed state
.

There is a bijective correspondence between the set of states
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
and
the set of density matrices
\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
, given by

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))\ni\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}}\leftrightarrow\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}})=\tr\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}}\quad\forall\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{M}}\in\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}).

Proposition 2.25

(Projection Lattice in
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
)
.

The projections
\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))\subset\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})_{+}
are a partially ordered set with
the ordering from Definition
2.12
, and may be given a
lattice structure
.
Let
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
be two orthogonal projections. The lattice structure
is established by
defining the
infimum
as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1}\sqcap\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2}:=\inf\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2}\}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\inf}
the
orthogonal projection
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\inf}:\mathbb{C}^{n}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1})\cap(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2})
, and as
supremum

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1}\sqcup\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2}:=\sup\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2}\}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\sup}

the orthogonal projection
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{\sup}:\mathbb{C}^{n}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\spn\{(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1})\cup(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2})\}=\spn\{(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{1})+(\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}_{2})\}
.
These definitions extend the ones which were given
in Proposition
2.19
for commuting subsets of
\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
.

It is fairly obvious that the negation or complement
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}^{\perp}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}-\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}
for
a
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}\in\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
is the orthogonal projection onto the kernel

\ker\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}
of
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}
, and
\ker\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}\oplus\im\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}=\mathbb{C}^{n}
. The greatest element in
the lattice is again
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{I}}
— the identity — and the least element is
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}

— the null matrix. This lattice is denoted as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}(\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})))
.

The
atoms
in this lattice (for an atom
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}(\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})))
there
is no distinct other element
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{{\mathsf{L}}}}(\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})))
such that

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}<\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{P}}<\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}
) are the minimal
projections of the form
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{Q}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}
with a unit vector
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{r}}\in\mathbb{C}^{n}
,
i.e.
\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{1}\subset\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))
(Proposition
2.24
).
Every projection of rank
m\leq n
can be expressed as the sum of
m
atomic projections
in
\mathrm{D}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C}))_{1}
.

Due to Zorn’s lemma, any commutative sub-algebra
\mathcal{C}
(e.g. a PVM-generated Abelian
algebra
\mathcal{C}=\spn\{\Uppi_{M}(E)\}
, cf. Definition
2.21
) can be embedded in or
extended to a MASA (maximal Abelian sub-algbra, cf. Definition
2.12
).
A commutative sub-algebra
\mathcal{C}
is a MASA
iff
it is unitarily equivalent
to the commutative algebra of diagonal matrices
\mathbb{D}_{n}(\mathbb{C})\subset\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
from
Example
4
, i.e.
\exists\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}\in\mathrm{U}(\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})):\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathcal{C}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{U}}=\mathbb{D}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
, e.g.
[
94
]
.

The advantage of an algebra is that all products and especially all powers are in the algebra.
As the state is defined on the whole probability algebra, this leads to the definition of moments:

Definition 2.26

(Moments)
.

The
moments
of order
n\in\mathbb{N}
of
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
are defined
as the numbers
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{M}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}_{n}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{n})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{n})
.
For any finite set of RVs
\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{j}\},j=1\dots m
, not necessarily distinct, and
which do not necessarily commute,
the
mixed moments
of order
n_{1},\dots,n_{m}\in\{1,\star\}
,
m\in\mathbb{N}
, are
defined as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{M}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}_{n_{1}\dots n_{m}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{1},\dots,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{m}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{1}^{n_{1}}\dots\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{m}^{n_{m}})
,
where the ordering of the elements matters for non-commutative algebras.

If for two random variables
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{1},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{2}
it holds that for all
n
the moments match,

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{M}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}_{n}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{1})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{M}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}_{n}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{2})
, denoting this as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{1}\overset{\text{m}}{=}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}_{2}
,
one says that they are
moment equivalent
.

Having defined the expectation of powers leading to moments, it is natural to extend
these definitions linearly to polynomials, leading to the definition of the
law or distribution of a RV:

Definition 2.27

(Law of a Random Variable)
.

For a RV
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
and a polynomial
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}\in\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{X}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}]
in one unknown
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{X}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}
,
one may compute
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}))
— e.g. with the help of the moments
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{M}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{M}}_{n}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})
. The

law of
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
is defined as the linear mapping
\tau_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}:\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{X}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}]\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathbb{C}
:

\tau_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}:\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}\mapsto\tau_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}))=\mathbb{E}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}))
.

Just as for mixed moments in Definition
2.26
, one can define the law of a collection
of non-commuting RVs by extending Definition
2.27
to
joint laws
, but this will
not be needed here any further. The following fact follows obviously from linearity:

Proposition 2.28
.

RVs with equal moments have equal laws, and they are moment equivalent.

As RVs in finite dimensional algebras are always bounded (cf. Definition
2.12
),
as will be seen shortly, it is convenient in the following to limit ourselves to bounded RVs.
From the kind of law defined in Definition
2.27
on polynomials one comes very quickly to
the classical notion of law as the distribution measure of a RV:

Theorem 2.29

(Distribution Law of a RV)
.

For any self-adjoint bounded RV
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}_{sa}
there is a
probability measure

\mu_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}
on
[-C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}},C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}]\subset\mathbb{R}
, where
C_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}

is a bounding constant of
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
as in Definition
2.12
(cf. Proposition
2.49
)
— also called the law or rather the
distribution (law)
of the RV
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
—
such that for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{p}}\in\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{X}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{X}}]
one has
