\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{b}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{a}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}:\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{x}}\mapsto(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{a}}^{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{H}}{\textstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{H}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{x}})\,\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{b}}
. The canonical basis
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{e}}_{i}
may just
be written as
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{e}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{e}}_{i}=\ket{i}
. A matrix
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}\in\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
can be written as

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{A}}=(A_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{n}=\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}A_{ij}\ket{i}\bra{j}
.

2.2
Representations and Hilbert Space

The concept of representation, representing the algebra
\mathcal{A}
as a sub-algebra of the
algebra of linear operators
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
on some vector space
\mathcal{H}
,
turns out to be of great importance in algebraic probability.

General Representations:

Definition 2.38

(Representation)
.

Let
\mathcal{H}
be a vector space, and
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
the algebra of linear maps
(operators) on
\mathcal{H}
.
A representation of an algebra
\mathcal{A}
is an algebra homomorphism
\Upsilon
of
\mathcal{A}
into

\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
, i.e.
\mathcal{A}\ni\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mapsto\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=:\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
.
This means that
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
is linear, and

\mathcal{A}\ni\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\mapsto\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
.
The subspace
\im\Upsilon=\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
is a sub-algebra of
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
.

For a unital algebra
\mathcal{A}
one obtains that
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}})=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}}
has to act
like the identity on
\im\Upsilon
.

In case
\mathcal{A}
is a *-algebra, and
\mathcal{H}
an inner product
(pre-Hilbert) space (cf. Example
15
),
then
\Upsilon
is a *-representation in case it is a *-homomorphism,
i.e. if in addition for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
one has

\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star})=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}}=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}^{\dagger}=\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})^{\dagger}
,
where
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}^{\dagger}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
is the adjoint of
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}
.

If
\Upsilon
is injective, the representation is called
faithful
. In this case
the sub-algebra
\im\Upsilon=\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
is isomorphic to
\mathcal{A}
.

We have already encountered observations or samples, i.e. non-zero *-homomorphisms
or characters onto
\mathbb{C}
in Definition
2.6
. These are one-dimensional
representations. One of the most natural ones is the regular representation:

Definition 2.39

(Regular Representation)
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be an algebra.
For each
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
, define a linear map
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})

for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}
by
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}
.
The homomorphism
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\ni\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mapsto\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
is
called the
(left) regular representation
.

As a concrete example, one might view Example
4
as the
regular representation of Example
2
.
The regular representation, Definition
2.39
, is faithful for unital algebras

[
55
]
:

Theorem 2.40

(Cayley)
.

Every unital algebra
\mathcal{A}
admits a faithful representation, e.g. via the regular
representation
\Upsilon
from Definition
2.39
. In other words, this means that
\mathcal{A}

is isomorphic with the sub-algebra
\im\Upsilon=\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
.

Proof.

If for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}
it holds for the regular representation (Definition
2.39
)
that
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}
in
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
,
then for a unital algebra
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}
,
and hence
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}
; proving that the regular representation is faithful.
∎

As the interest here is mainly on *-representations, the focus will be in the sequel
on cases where the undelying vector space
\mathcal{H}
can be equipped with a Hilbert
space structure, cf. Definition
2.38
. To exclude many almost pathological
situations, for the sake of simplicity one may also assume that the algebra
is a Banach *-algebra (cf. Definition
2.60
).

Proposition 2.41

(Proper or Non-degenerate Representation)
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be a Banach *-algebra,

\mathcal{H}
a Hilbert space, and
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
a *-representation.
Then the following are equivalent (cf.
[
138
]
):

•

\spn\{\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\xi\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A},\,\xi\in\mathcal{H}\}
is dense in
\mathcal{H}
.

•

For any non-zero
\xi\in\mathcal{H}
, there exists an
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
such that

\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\xi\neq 0
.

If either one of these conditions is satisfied, the representation

\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H})
is said to be
proper
or
non-degenerate
.

Later in the GNS-construction to follow in Theorem
2.53
,
the state will become a pure state, defined by a cyclic and separating vector,
so we define this for any representation:

Definition 2.42

(Cyclic and Separating Vector)
.

A representation
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
as in Proposition
2.41
,
with
\mathcal{H}
a Hilbert space, is
called a
cyclic
representation (cf. Example
15
)
iff

there is a unit vector
\xi\in\mathcal{H}
, also called a
cyclic vector
,
such that the
orbit

\{\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\xi\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}\}\subset\mathcal{H}

is
dense
in
\mathcal{H}
.

A unit vector
\xi\in\mathcal{H}
is called a
separating
vector for the representation

\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})

iff
for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
it holds that

\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\xi=0
implies
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
.

Note that a cyclic representation is proper or non-degenerate, and that observations
(if they exist) are cyclic.

Definition 2.43

(Irreducible Representation)
.

Given a representation
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
as in Proposition
2.41
,
with
\mathcal{H}
a Hilbert space, a closed subspace
\mathcal{K}\subset\mathcal{H}
is
called an
invariant
subspace of the representation
\Upsilon
,

iff

\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})(\mathcal{K})\subseteq\mathcal{K}
for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
. In this
case the restriction
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})|_{\mathcal{K}}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K})
yields a

sub-representation
of
\Upsilon
on the Hilbert space
\mathcal{K}
. And it is easy
to see that the orthogonal complement
\mathcal{K}^{\perp}\subset\mathcal{H}
is also an invariant
subspace of the representation
\Upsilon
, so that

\Upsilon=\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})|_{\mathcal{K}}\oplus\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})|_{\mathcal{K}^{\perp}}
, i.e. the representation

\Upsilon
is the
direct sum
(cf. Definition
2.70
) of two sub-representations.

If the only invariant subspaces of the representation
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})

are
\{0\}
and
\mathcal{H}
, the representation is called
irreducible
; otherwise
it is called
reducible
.

It should be obvious that a cyclic representation (cf. Definition
2.42
)
is irreducible. In fact one has
[
94
]
:

Theorem 2.44

(Schur’s Lemma)
.

For a representation
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
as in Proposition
2.41

with
\mathcal{H}
a Hilbert space,
irreducibility
(Definition
2.43
) is
equivalent to each of the following statements:

•

Any unit vector
\xi\in\mathcal{H}
is a
cyclic vector
for
\Upsilon

(cf. Definition
2.42
);

•

\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})^{\prime}=\mathbb{C}[I]
— the commutant
\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})^{\prime}
(Definition
2.12
)
of the image
\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})
are just the multiples of the identity,
this is called
Schur’s lemma
.

Irreducible representations are the basic building blocks
of general representations:

Proposition 2.45

(Sum of Cyclic Representations)
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be a Banach *-algebra (cf. Definition
2.60
),

\mathcal{H}
a Hilbert space, and assume that

\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
a proper, nondegenerate *-representation,
cf. Proposition
2.41
. Then (cf.
[
138
]
) it is
the
direct sum
(cf. Definition
2.43
) of
cyclic representations
,
cf. Definition
2.42
.

It is fairly obvious by now that any finite dimensional algebra
\mathcal{A}
is isomorphic to a sub-algebra
of
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
of Example
14
.

Remark 2.46

(Matrix Algebra Representation)
.

Often one starts out from the regular representation Definition
2.39
.
Then it all comes down to a choice of basis, and there is in general no canonical
way of doing so.
A path which works in any algebra is
using the structure constants in Definition
2.14
.
But here we shall stay with the more restricted situation involving an
underlying Hilbert space structure, see also Example
15
and the
resulting Remark
2.35
.

There are other ways of achieving a matrix representations
[
138
]
, but
they are connected to the structure theorems to be discussed later in
Section
2.3
. Before refining the foregoing to the case of probability
algebras, it is worthwhile to take a closer look at the states
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})\subset\mathcal{A}^{+}
.

States of the Probability Algebra:

In the previous representation results, Theorem
2.40
and Remark
2.46
,
the representation was for valid for any algebra,
independent of the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
which defines probabilities.

To achieve a representation on a Hilbert space which takes care
of this, one has to consider the given state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}
, to which we turn next.
Consider the dual space
\mathcal{A}^{\star}
of
\mathcal{A}
. Any
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\star}
defines a
sesqui-linear form
b
on
\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{A}
— linear in the second argument and
anti-linear in the first — and a linear map
B:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{A}^{\star}
:

\forall\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}:\,b(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle=:\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle,

(2.15)

where one may recall that
\left\langle\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle
is the duality bracket on
\mathcal{A}^{\star}\times\mathcal{A}
.

For a such a map
B\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\star})
, in reflexive situations where

(\mathcal{A}^{\star})^{\star}\cong\mathcal{A}
as for finite dimensional algebras,
one may view the transpose or dual map
B^{*}\in\mathcal{L}((\mathcal{A}^{\star})^{\star},\mathcal{A}^{\star})

as a map
B^{*}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\star})\cong\mathcal{L}((\mathcal{A}^{\star})^{\star},\mathcal{A}^{\star})
.
The map
B\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\star})
is called self-dual
(or sometimes self-adjoint)
if
B^{*}=B
. Complementing Definition
2.1
, one is lead to

Definition 2.47
.

In case
B
is
self-dual
(or self-adjoint),
i.e.
\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle=\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\right\rangle=\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}^{\star},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\rangle^{*}
,
then
b
and
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}
are called self-adjoint (Hermitean), the self-adjoint functionals
are denoted by
\mathcal{A}^{sa}\subset\mathcal{A}^{\star}
. This means that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})
is real on
self-adjoint
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
; for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}
one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathcal{A}_{sa})\subseteq\mathbb{R}
.

For
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\star}
one may define an involution
\natural:\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\mapsto\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}^{\natural}

such that for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}^{\natural}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star})^{*}
.
For self-adjoint
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}
one has
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}^{\natural}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}
.

In case a self-dual
B
is
positive
(
\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\rangle\geq 0
),
the same is attached to
b
and
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}
, and in case

B
is
positive definite
(
\left\langle B\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\rangle>0
for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\neq\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
),
so is
b
and
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}
.

All such positive
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}\subseteq\mathcal{A}^{\star}
form a convex cone,
the
dual cone

\mathcal{A}^{+}:=\{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}\mid\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\rangle=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\geq 0\quad\forall\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}_{+}\}
,
dual to the positive cone
\mathcal{A}_{+}
, cf. Definition
2.12
.

One may recall, cf. Definition
2.1
, that a self-adjoint and positive
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\star}

is called a
state
, and if it is additionally positive
definite,
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}
is also called
faithful
, and
normalised
if
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}})=1
.

Note that the definition of the sesqui-linear form in Eq.(
2.15
)
is sometimes the other way around, i.e. linear
in the first argument and anti-linear in the second.

Proposition 2.48

(Geometry of the Set of States)
.

The self-adjoint functionals
\mathcal{A}^{sa}\subset\mathcal{A}^{\star}
are a real vector space, and it
holds that
\mathcal{A}^{\star}=\mathcal{A}^{sa}\oplus\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathrm{i}}{\textstyle\mathrm{i}}{\scriptstyle\mathrm{i}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{i}}\mathcal{A}^{sa}
as a direct sum over
\mathbb{R}
, as well as

\mathcal{A}^{\star}=\spn_{\mathbb{C}}\mathcal{A}^{sa}
, i.e. any functional is the complex linear combination
of two self-adjoint functionals, cf. Definition
2.12
.

The dual positive cone
\mathcal{A}^{+}\subset\mathcal{A}^{\star}
is a
generating
cone, i.e.
\mathcal{A}^{sa}=\mathcal{A}^{+}-\mathcal{A}^{+}
over
\mathbb{R}
and
\mathcal{A}^{\star}=\mathcal{A}^{+}-\mathcal{A}^{+}
over
\mathbb{C}
.
This means that any element
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}\in\mathcal{A}^{sa}
is the difference of two positive
elements (corresponding to the
Jordan decomposition
of measures):

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}-\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}
with
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\psi}}\in\mathcal{A}^{+}
, and hence any functional

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\star}
is the complex combination of four positive elements in
\mathcal{A}^{+}
,
cf. Definition
2.12
.

The elements
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\star}
which satisfy
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}})=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\right\rangle=1

form a hyperplane
\mathcal{T}\subset\mathcal{A}^{\star}
. Thus the set of normalised states

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{T}\cap\mathcal{A}^{+}
is a convex set lying in the linear manifold
\mathcal{T}
.
Its extreme points are called

pure states
, all other states are called
mixed states
.
Vector states (cf. Example
15
) are pure states,
as are characters
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{X}}{\textstyle\mathsf{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{X}}(\mathcal{A})\subset\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
, if
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{X}}{\textstyle\mathsf{X}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{X}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{X}}(\mathcal{A})
is non-empty.

For more information on the geometry of the set of states, see
[
17
]
.
The next task is to define a trace functional on an abstract algebra
\mathcal{A}
:

Proposition 2.49

(Trace on
\mathcal{A}
)
.

In case
\mathcal{A}
is a finite dimensional algebra, one has that
\mathcal{A}=\mathrm{B}(\mathcal{A})
,
as from Theorem
2.40
one sees that
\mathcal{A}
is isomorphic to a sub-algebra
of
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})
, the linear maps of a finite dimensional space, as
on finite dimensional spaces all linear maps are bounded and continuous
[
120
]
.

Now by the same argument as in Proposition
2.34
, there is a unique tracial linear
functional
\tr
on
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})
, normalised to

\tr(I_{\mathcal{A}})=\dim\mathcal{A}
. This one may use, via the faithful
regular representation
\Upsilon:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
from Definition
2.39
, to define the trace functional
\tr_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathcal{A}^{+}
on
\mathcal{A}
by setting

\tr_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}):=\tr\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}
, or, more formally,
\tr_{\mathcal{A}}:=\tr\circ\Upsilon
.
In the sequel it is assumed that
{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 2.58334pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\kern-1.50696pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-1.29167pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\textstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.01385pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}}\,\tr_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is non-degenerate (cf. Remark
2.15
),
resp. a faithful state (cf. Proposition
2.16
).

For a unital algebra one has that

\tr_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}})=\tr(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}})=\tr(I)=\dim\mathcal{A}
.
and hence, according to Remark
2.2
, for a *-algebra
\mathcal{A}
,

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{c}:={\mathchoice{{{{\raise 2.58334pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\kern-1.50696pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-1.29167pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\textstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.01385pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle(\dim\mathcal{A})$}}}}}}}}\,\tr_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is a faithful
canonical state on
\mathcal{A}
.

Associated Hilbert Space Representation:

The Remark
2.35
and Remark
2.46
show how to map
a finite dimensional algebra onto a
matrix algebra. To achieve a *-representation for a unital *-algebra
\mathcal{A}
, one
proceeds via a Hilbert space construction, and an associated representation,
the so-called GNS (Gel’fand - Neumark (Naĭmark)) - Segal)
construction
[
63
,
131
,
54
]
.

Proposition 2.50

(Associated Hilbert Space)
.

Given a probability algebra
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
with a faithful state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
,
define a positive definite sesqui-linear form
on
\mathcal{A}
like in Eq.(
2.15
), denoted as

\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle_{2}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})
, an
inner product
.

With this inner product,
\mathcal{A}
becomes a pre-Hilbert space, and we denote its
Hilbert space completion by
\mathcal{H}_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}}:=\mathrm{L}_{2}(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
, or by

\mathscr{H}=\mathrm{L}_{2}(\mathcal{A})
for short if it is clear from the context which state

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is meant.
This is the Hilbert space associated with the probability algebra
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
.
The associated Hilbert norm is denoted by

\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\|_{2}:=\sqrt{\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\right\rangle_{2}}
.

The direct sum
\mathcal{A}=\,\overline{\!{\mathcal{A}}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}
from Definition
2.12
becomes
an
orthogonal
direct sum, as with
\,\overline{\!{\mathcal{A}}}=\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}]
for
\widetilde{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\in\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}

one has
\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\mid\widetilde{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\right\rangle_{2}:=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\widetilde{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\widetilde{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}})=0
.
This orthogonal decomposition can be extended to
\mathscr{H}=\,\overline{\!{\mathscr{H}}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathscr{H}}
, with

\,\overline{\!{\mathscr{H}}}=\,\overline{\!{\mathcal{A}}}=\mathbb{C}[\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}]
and
\widetilde{\mathscr{H}}
the completion of
\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}
.

In case
\mathcal{A}
is finite dimensional, it is already complete in all vector
Hausdorff topologies
[
120
]
, and thus one has
\mathscr{H}=\mathcal{A}
in this instance.
Generally,
\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathscr{H}
is a dense subspace, and
the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}
may be extended to
\mathscr{H}
by continuity.

One such faithful (but un-normalised) state on a finite dimensional unital *-algebra
\mathcal{A}

is the trace functional
\tr_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathcal{A}^{+}
introduced in Proposition
2.49
.
This may be used to introduce an alternative inner product on
\mathcal{A}
:

Remark 2.51

(Canonical Associated Finite Dimensional Hilbert Space)
.

For a finite dimensional *-algebra
\mathcal{A}
,
according to Proposition
2.34
, the trace on
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
induces
the
Hilbert-Schmidt
inner product
\left\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\right\rangle_{HS}
on
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
.
Via the trace
\tr_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathcal{A}^{+}
considered in Proposition
2.49

for this finite dimensional case,
a
canonical
inner product on
\mathcal{A}
may be introduced:

\forall\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}:\;\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle_{c}:=\tr_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}),

making the finite dimensional unital *-algebra
\mathcal{A}
into a Hilbert space

(\mathcal{A},\left\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\right\rangle_{c})
, which will be denoted by
\mathcal{H}_{c}
.
The regular representation Definition
2.39

then satisfies following relation: for all
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{H}_{c}
,

\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle_{c}=\tr_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})=\tr(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}})=\tr(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}^{\dagger}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}})=\left\langle\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mid\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}\right\rangle_{HS},

where the adjoint
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}^{\dagger}
is w.r.t.
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{c})
.
This means that
\Upsilon
is a unitary map between
the Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{c}
and the Hilbert sub-space

\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})
of
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
with the Hilbert-Schmidt inner
product
\left\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\right\rangle_{HS})
, cf. Proposition
2.34
.

The connected canonical Frobenius state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{c}
defined
in Proposition
2.49
on
\mathcal{A}
is obviously a faithful state,
so that all the statements from Proposition
2.50
apply
to
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{c})
.

Not surprisingly, Remark
2.36
for Example
15
and
Remark
2.32
for Example
14
have a version for
finite dimensional *-algebras:

Remark 2.52

(Algebra Schatten Norms)
.

In case
\mathcal{A}
is a finite dimensional *-algebra, following Proposition
2.49
,
for each
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\in\mathcal{A}
and any
p\geq 1
one may define the
Schatten-
p
-norm

\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\|_{Sp}:=\left(\tr\left[(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}^{\star}}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}})^{{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 1.80835pt\hbox{{$\textstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.75346pt\hbox{\kern-1.05487pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-0.90417pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 2$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.1097pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.60275pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.60275pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 2$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.2604pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 2$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.2604pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 2$}}}}}}}}}\right]\right)^{{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 1.80835pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.75346pt\hbox{\kern-1.05487pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-0.90417pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\textstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.1097pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.60275pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.60275pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.2604pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.2604pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}}}}}}}=\left(\tr\left[(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}^{\dagger}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}})^{{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 1.80835pt\hbox{{$\textstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.75346pt\hbox{\kern-1.05487pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-0.90417pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 2$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 2.1097pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle p$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 2$}}}}}}}}}\right]\right)^{{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 1.80835pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.51234pt\hbox{\kern-1.35623pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.45206pt\hbox{\kern-1.20552pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}}}}}}},

(2.16)

and extend this to
p=\infty
by setting
\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\|_{S\infty}:=\left\|\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}\right\|_{\infty}
,
i.e. the
operator norm
of
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})
.
Note that the Schatten-2-norm
\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\|_{S2}=\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\|_{c}

is equal to the norm from the canonical inner product from Remark
2.51
.

The norm
\left\|\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\|_{S1}
is again called the
trace norm
or
nuclear norm
.
And as
Banach spaces
,
(\mathcal{A},\left\|\cdot\right\|_{Sp})
and

(\mathcal{A},\left\|\cdot\right\|_{Sq})
with
{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 2.58334pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\kern-1.50696pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-1.29167pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\textstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.01385pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle p$}}}}}}}}+{\mathchoice{{{{\raise 2.58334pt\hbox{{$\textstyle 1$}}}{\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\kern-1.50696pt\hbox{/}}}{\raise-1.29167pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\textstyle q$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.01385pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{\footnotesize/}}}{\raise-0.86108pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptstyle q$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\scriptsize/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle q$}}}}}}}{{{{\raise 3.22916pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle 1$}}}{\raise 0.73193pt\hbox{\kern-1.93747pt\hbox{\tiny/}}}{\raise-0.6458pt\hbox{\kern-1.72218pt\hbox{{$\scriptscriptstyle q$}}}}}}}}=1
are
dual

to each other. With the operator- or Schatten-
\infty
-norm,

(\mathcal{A},\left\|\cdot\right\|_{\infty})
is a
Banach algebra
(cf. Definition
2.60
).

Let
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}})
be a probability algebra. In order to achieve a faithful
Hilbert space representation, a faithful state is necessary. To this end define

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}=\begin{cases}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}&\text{if $\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}$ is faithful}.\\
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{c}&\text{from Proposition\penalty\ \ref{prop:fin-dim-alg-gen} otherwise}.\end{cases}

(2.17)

This ensures that
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is a faithful state. Using this
state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
from Eq.(
2.17
), by now considering
the probability algebra
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
, one may now formulate a finite
dimensional Hilbert space representation as the
simplified version of a basic GNS (Gel’fand - Neumark (Naĭmark)) - Segal)
construction
[
63
,
131
,
54
]
:

Theorem 2.53

(Finite Dimensional GNS Construction)
.

Let
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
be a probability algebra where all elements are bounded
\mathcal{A}=\mathrm{B}(\mathcal{A})

— e.g. when
\mathcal{A}
is finite dimensional — with
a faithful state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
, and according to Proposition
2.50

form the Hilbert space
\mathscr{H}
with inner product
\left\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\right\rangle_{2}
through
completion. Combine this with the regular representation Definition
2.39
to achieve
a faithful *-representation
\Upsilon:\,\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{H})
, cf. Definition
2.38
,
with
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{*}\mapsto\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star})=\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})^{\dagger}
, where
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})^{\dagger}

is the Hilbert space adjoint to
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})
w.r.t.
\left\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\right\rangle_{2}
.
In other words,
\mathcal{A}
is *-isomorphic to
\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{L}(\mathscr{H})
.

In this associated Hilbert space framework, note that for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{x}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}\in\mathscr{H}
:

\mathbb{E}_{2}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{x}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}):=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{x}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{x}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{x}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{x}})=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{x}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{x}}\right\rangle_{2},

(2.18)

with
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}
continuously extended to
\mathscr{H}
.
Hence, as
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
, one obtains

\mathbb{E}_{\Upsilon}(\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}):=\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\mid\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\right\rangle_{2},

(2.19)

to define the corresponding
vector state

\mathbb{E}_{\Upsilon}
on
\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{H})
.
This means that the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
has been mapped onto a
vector

or
pure state
for this representation in the associated Hilbert space algebra

\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subset\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{H})
with state vector
\xi=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\in\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathscr{H}
.
Note that the two random variables
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}
and
\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\in\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})

are
moment equivalent
,
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\overset{\text{m}}{=}\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}
.

The vector
\xi=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\in\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathscr{H}
in Eq.(
2.19
)
is a
separating
vector for
\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})
,
which according to Definition
2.42
means that if
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}
,
then
\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{0}}
, which is the case only for
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{0}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{0}}
.

The regular representation on
\mathscr{H}
just so constructed is also a
cyclic

representation (cf. Definition
2.42
),
as
\{\Upsilon(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}})\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\in\mathcal{A}\}=\mathcal{A}
is by definition dense in
\mathscr{H}
.
The vector
\xi=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{1}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{1}}\in\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathscr{H}
is hence a
cyclic
unit vector.

One may recall that a vector state like Eq.(
2.19
) is a pure state
of
\mathcal{L}(\mathscr{H})
, so this is an example of
purification
, achieved through
what is called the “Church of the Larger Hilbert Space”

[
134
]
(cf. also
[
97
]
).
It is accomplished through a representation in a “larger” Hilbert space, or rather
by embedding it as a sub-algebra
\Upsilon(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{L}(\mathscr{H})
of a “larger” algebra.
For such a state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\beta}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}):=\left\langle\xi\mid\Upsilon_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}}\,\xi\right\rangle_{2}
, given as a vector state with
a normalised vector
\xi\in\mathscr{H}
as in Eq.(
2.19
) in the above Theorem
2.53
,
the vector
\xi
itself is called a state or state vector
(of some system), and in fact this is the original use of the term “state”.

In Theorem
2.53
a specific Hilbert space
\mathscr{H}
was constructed from the algebra
\mathcal{A}

itself via the regular representation. But the idea of a faithful pure representation
is so useful, that one wants to use the term more generally:

Definition 2.54

(GNS-Representation)
.

Let there be given a probability algebra
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
and a

faithful representation

\Psi:\mathcal{A}\>\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 4.49588pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 14.99176pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces}}}}\>\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
of
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
in

(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}),\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{\xi})
, where, as in Example
15
,

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{\xi}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}))
is the
pure vector state

\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{\xi}(A)=\left\langle\xi\mid A\xi\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}}
for
A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
.
Moreover, the vector
\xi\in\mathcal{H}
is assumed to be a
cyclic unit vector

for
\Psi(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})
in the Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}
.
Then the tuple
(\Psi,\mathcal{H},\xi)
resp.
(\Psi,\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}),\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\omega}}_{\xi})

is called a
GNS-representation
of
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}})
.

For the GNS-representations from Theorem
2.53
, there is also a matrix representation
on
\mathbb{M}_{n}(\mathbb{C})
to parallel Remark
2.35
, and one does not have
to use the structure constants explicitly as in Remark
2.46
.

\mathcal{A}\cong\mathchoice{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}^{{\kern-27.92017pt{B}\kern 23.84653pt}}}{\hphantom{{}^{{{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\textstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfbfit{H}}^{{\kern-27.92017pt{B}\kern are *-isomorphic.

In Theorem
2.53
and up to here it was ensured through Eq.(
2.17
)
that the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}\in\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsf{S}}{\textstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptstyle\mathsf{S}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{S}}(\mathcal{A})
is faithful, even if the original state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}

of the probability algebra
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}})
were not faithful.
What Theorem
2.53
shows is that the GNS-construction then yields a faithful, cyclic
(cf. Definition
2.42
), and hence irreducible (cf. Definition
2.43
)
representation.

In case the original state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}
of
(\mathcal{A},\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}})
is not faithful,
and one were to form the sesqui-linear form
\left\langle\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}\mid\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}\right\rangle_{\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}(\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{a}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{a}}^{\star}\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{b}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{b}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{b}})
,
this would not be an inner product, as it would not be positive definite

\left\|\cdot\right\|_{2}
would not be a norm, and it could not be used to define a
Hilbert space structure on
\mathcal{A}
in Proposition
2.50
.
For such a state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}
which is not faithful
and the choice
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\varpi}}=\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\phi}}_{c}
was taken in Eq.(
2.17
),
the inner product on
\mathscr{H}=\mathcal{H}_{c}
is not connected to the probability
structure defined by the state
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\textstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}{\scriptscriptstyle\mathsfit{\alpha}}
. One may stay with this representation
on
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{c})
, and compute expectations using densities
\mathchoice{\displaystyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\textstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol{R}}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{c})

(cf. Corollary
